title: Long Have I Sat Beneath the Sound
description: Long Have I Sat Beneath the Sound in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 165, headed “Unfruitfulness, ignorance, and unsanctified affections”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Long have I sat be-neath the sound Of thy sal-va-tion, Lord But still how weak my faith is found, And knowl-edge of thy word!

lines: Long have I sat beneath the sound
Of thy salvation, Lord
But still how weak my faith is found,
And knowledge of thy word!
Oft I frequent thy holy place
And hear almost in vain;
How small a portion of thy grace
My memory can retain!
My dear Almighty, and my God,
How little art thou known
By all the judgments of thy rod,
And blessings of thy throne!
How cold and feeble is my love!
How negligent my fear!
How low my hope of joys above!
How few affections there!
Great God, thy sovereign power impart
To give thy word success:
Write the salvation in my heart,
And make me learn the grace.
Shew my forgetful feet the way
That leads to joys on high;
There knowledge grows without decay,
And love shall never die.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
